title: Tenant credit pools and soft-degrade orchestration for cross-region failovers
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: During regional capacity stress or partial outages we need a predictable way to keep high-SLAs online while degrading lower-tier traffic, without hard-killing requests or incurring regulatory/data locality violations. Existing lane-based shedding prototypes work well for instantaneous spikes but do not account for historical SLA consumption, cross-region failover cost, or graceful soft-degrades that preserve useful UX (partial answers, structured fallbacks).

Goal: Implement a tenant-level credit banking system (Tenant Credit Pools) combined with a soft-degrade orchestrator that: 1) preserves per-tenant SLOs where possible by prioritizing requests based on remaining credits, 2) enables controlled cross-region failover that can borrow/transfer credits under operator policy, and 3) exposes degradation modes (truncation, lightweight model variants, cached stub responses, early-ack + background completion) selectable per policy. Integrate with circuit-breakers so that when a region's health crosses thresholds, the orchestrator can switch from admission-based shedding to circuit-breaker-driven re-routing while honoring tenant credits and data locality constraints.

Why different: Unlike prior designs that are purely queue-time or probability-based shedders, this design accounts for temporal SLA consumption (credits decay/refresh), supports credit handoff during multi-region failover, and couples admissions with explicit graceful degradation modes instead of only dropping or truncating responses. This should reduce P0 customer impact and provide clearer billing/transparent behavior during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant Credit Pool created per tenant with configurable monthly credit allotment and decay policy
Admission controller consults Tenant Credit Pool and priority policy to accept, defer, or downgrade incoming requests
Orchestrator supports at least three soft-degrade actions: response truncation, model-slimming (smaller variant), and cached-stub response
Cross-region failover path can request temporary credit loans with operator-configurable global caps and audit logs
Circuit-breaker integration: when region health is degraded, new requests are automatically routed with preserved credit-ordering and degradation mode selection
End-to-end tests validating that high-SLA tenants keep >=95% of requests accepted under synthetic region stress while low-SLA tenants receive graceful degradation behaviors
Metrics and dashboards: per-tenant credit balance, borrow events, degrade-mode counts, acceptance rates and P50/P95 latency by degrade-mode
Feature flag gated rollout and kill-switch with immediate reversion to existing shedding policy
design_decisions: Credit model: monthly allotment with linear decay; unused credits do not roll over more than one cycle
Admission algorithm: score = priority_weight * (remaining_credits / allotment) - cost_estimate; accept if score >= threshold, else attempt downgrade or queue
Degradation precedence: try lightweight model variant -> truncation -> cached-stub -> early-ack background-completion
Cross-region borrowing: coordinator requests loan from destination region's operator pool; loans are small, timeboxed, and auditable
Circuit-breaker handoff: use existing region-health stream; on tripping, orchestrator switches to loan-first mode with accelerated degrade-mode selection
Security/data locality: tuner to mark tenants as non-eligible for cross-region loans if their data controls disallow it
tradeoffs_considered: Aggressive borrowing reduces dropped requests but increases cross-region egress and potential compliance risk
Fine-grained credits per endpoint increase control but add storage/latency overhead to admissions path
Background completion (early-ack) improves perceived latency but complicates idempotency and billing calculations
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + datastore for Tenant Credit Pools; simple linear decay and admin UI to set allotments
Phase 2: Integrate credit check into admission path with a mock degrade-mode selection (truncate only) behind feature flag
Phase 3: Add model-variant selection and cached-stub integration; instrumentation & dashboards
Phase 4: Cross-region loan coordinator and circuit-breaker handoff; security opt-outs
Phase 5: Canary rollout (10% traffic) -> 50% -> global with progressive policy tightening and SLO monitoring
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit arithmetic, decay, and loan settlement
Integration tests simulating regional failure and verifying loan flow and audit logs
Chaos experiment: lose 1 AZ then 1 region in staging and assert degrade-mode transitions and SLO preservation
Load tests: ensure admission decision path adds <2ms p95 overhead under 2000 rps per shard
User-acceptance: sample customers simulate failover on test tenants to validate UX of early-ack and stub responses
observability_requirements: Alerts: credit_balance < 10% for high-SLA tenants, loan_failure_rate > 0.5% within 5m
Trace spans for admission decision including credit lookup latency and degrade-mode decision path
rollout_plan: Feature flag default off in prod; enable for internal tenants
Canary 1: small set of internal customers with varied SLO tiers for 72h
Canary 2: selected external tenants who opt-in via Support and signed agreement for loan behavior
Full rollout contingent on <0.5% unexpected error rate and acceptance rates meeting SLO targets for canary group
